verdicts.why: Seed target 'I didn't want to ask you' renders 'nicht' as the contraction in 'didn't'; 'not' is not a contiguous substring but the row belongs to its own LEGO.
'gemacht' is rendered as 'do' in 'didn't do much'; 'done' is the participle form of a word that is in the sentence.
Seed 'I saw them' renders 'gesehen' as 'saw'; 'seen' is the participle of a word in the sentence.
'nicht' is rendered as the contraction in 'didn't do much'; 'not' is a literal gloss of a word that is present in contracted form.
Seed 'I'd like you to tell me' does not render 'dass' as 'that'; the row is a literal gloss of a dropped particle.
Seed 'I'll be able to speak' contains 'will' only as the contraction 'I'll'; 'will' is fused, not a substring.
Seed 'I saw them' renders perfect 'habe...gesehen' as simple past, so 'have' is not rendered; it is a literal gloss of the auxiliary.
Seed 'I don't mind' renders 'macht...aus' idiomatically; 'out' is a literal gloss of the separable particle.
Seed 'Did you have to finish' has 'had to' only as 'Did ... have to', interposed by 'you'; the LEGO is 'did you have to'.
Seed 'you'll be ready' contains 'will' only fused in the contraction 'you'll'.
Seed 'didn't know' contains 'know'; 'knew' is the past-tense form of a word in the sentence.
Seed 'What do you want me to do' has no 'that'; the row glosses a particle the translation dropped.

'ihr'/'her' appears nowhere in the seed 'Wirst du mir helfen...' or its LEGOs, but it is attached to LEGO 2 'helfen' and its practice sample is about another sentence; cutting is not provable here so it is left for judgement.
Seed 'used to know' contains 'know'; 'knew' is the past-tense form of a word in the sentence.
Seed 'wouldn't have said' has 'not' only fused in the contraction 'wouldn't'.
Seed 'I don't mind' does not render 'mir' as 'me'; the idiom drops it, so the row is a literal gloss.
Seed 'didn't know' renders 'nicht' as the contraction; 'not' is a literal gloss of a word present in fused form.
Seed 'Most people I know' renders 'die meisten' as 'most' with no 'the'; the row glosses a word the translation dropped.
Seed 'I don't mind' renders 'nichts' only via the idiom; 'nothing' is a literal gloss.
Seed 'I don't want to stop talking' renders 'nicht' as the contraction 'don't'; 'not' is a literal gloss of a fused word.
